technical_complexity.rationale: Extracting metrics from offering memorandums and data rooms into auditable Excel models is standard LLM engineering; secondaries add compliance and transfer restriction work.

defensibility.rationale: Marketplace liquidity could build a network over time, but at founding the claimed 40 accredited investors and $1.5M sourced were small, and well funded platforms and Excel AI startups already existed.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents consolidated into Schwab and Morgan Stanley in 2025 to 2026 per press, which strengthens rivals rather than copying the AI diligence wedge.

market_need_then: PitchBook estimated US VC secondaries traded about $106.3B in 2025, and companies stayed private longer, creating demand for liquidity.

branding.domain_note: Uses alt-x.co, not alt-x.com; the site title read 'Alt-X Perpetuals' when fetched, suggesting a mismatch with the described product.

identity.voice_and_tone: finance and AI positioning with changing taglines

brand_strength.rationale: Several taglines in circulation (liquidity layer, Excel agent) and the name collides with AltX, a separate alternatives data platform.

outcome_analysis: Alt-X is a Winter 2026 company whose two Stanford and Cornell computer science founders pitch AI infrastructure for private markets, with the CEO coming from Citadel. Early traction is self reported and small, and the product description has shifted between a secondaries venue and an Excel modeling agent. No outcome has occurred; competition from consolidated secondary platforms and funded Excel AI startups is the main risk.
notes: Funding unverified: trackers list $500K total (VCBacked says pre-seed announced Dec 2025, YC as investor); no announcement found, so no round recorded. YC pages conflict on batch (W26 versus F25) and founding year; directory gives Winter 2026. Traction figures are company claims. Completeness pass: the $500K pre-seed dated December 2025 is now recorded from VCBacked alone; another listing labels it seed. No announcement found.
